issues.description: GIT_MERGE.md remains not executable verbatim from a secondary worktree -- already filed as ISS-0023 (GitHub #81), re-confirmed here rather than re-filed. Two clauses again could not be followed literally. (1) Step 2 mandates 'git add -A', which this run's dispatch explicitly forbids because the sibling worktree shares the same .git; every file was staged by explicit path instead. (2) Step 9 mandates 'git checkout main' + 'git pull --ff-only origin main' + 'git branch -d', which is structurally impossible when local main is checked out in the sibling worktree; the equivalent used here was 'git fetch origin main --prune && git checkout --detach origin/main', which satisfies the protocol's intent (return to a clean, current base) without ever touching the local main ref. The protocol's acceptance criterion 'git branch --show-current is main' therefore cannot be met literally in a worktree, and its 'gh pr merge exited 0' criterion cannot be met either, since gh exits 1 on the local-checkout step after the API merge has already succeeded. This is the third run (REQ-022, REQ-023, now REQ-027) to record the same deviation, which strengthens the case for ISS-0023's documented worktree variant.

No new defects were found by this step. Recording for the audit trail that the dispatch's contingency conflict-resolution instructions did not engage: origin/main did not move between ORCH's pre-dispatch fetch and this step's own re-fetch (both fc88355), the merge-base was origin/main itself, and the rebase replayed nothing. lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex, handoffs/registry.json, docs/status/requirement_status.yaml, handoffs/orchestrator.log and docs/requirements.yaml were therefore all left exactly as the branch already had them -- no merge resolution was performed on any of them, and no entry from any side could have been dropped.
